title: From Mani Singh’s Death to the Wider Persecution of the Khalsa

blocks.text: This page is a hinge between two narrative movements. It first recalls that Mani Singh accepted death after recognizing the weight of the Sikhs’ curse and that his body was carried to Nikhas Chowk Lahore, where the sentence was fulfilled as a public warning.

The text then notes that companions with Mani Singh were also seized and executed, widening the tragedy beyond one celebrated martyr. Their deaths show that the authorities intended to punish an entire community rather than a single defiant leader.

From there the poem opens the next episode by broadening into a survey of state persecution under Khan Bahadur and Zakariya Khan. Different methods of execution, mutilation, and terror are introduced so that Mani Singh’s shahidi becomes the prelude to a longer campaign against the Khalsa.
